protocol_deviations: Field selection: the issue text lists only <ref> ==/!= <json> and count(<ref>) comparisons, but its own mandated reference-Program-B line IF V.tests.status != "passed" STOP failed(V.tests) requires reading the status field of the committed V.tests node. docs/spec/01-language-and-state.md explicitly allows 'immutable field selection' in control expressions, so dotted refs resolve as longest-committed-prefix + trailing field path (validation accepts any dotted prefix; evaluation fails the run loudly on a non-mapping node or missing field). A full dotted ref that exists as a node outright still resolves directly.

A bare unconditional terminal RETURN/STOP is still required by validation: a conditional STOP/RETURN is a possible exit, not a guaranteed one, so a program ending only in conditionals is rejected ('program requires a terminal RETURN or STOP'). Reference Program B, flattened to single lines, satisfies this naturally.

Conditional-DO targets are checked for duplicates but never added to the validation 'available' set: statically the branch may not run, so later statements cannot reference its nodes (returning or consuming a conditional branch's target requires routing through refs that unconditionally exist).

Crash-resume interplay is best-effort: resume of a program whose conditional-DO branch evaluated false pre-crash can leave an orphan PENDING task (resume.py, which this run must not modify, pre-creates tasks for every plan entry), and a skipped conditional followed by a fired one makes resume refuse safely with its existing mismatch guard. Fresh runs and non-conditional programs are unaffected; both resume smoke paths (crash before a true branch) pass.
Conditionals inside protocol files are validated per-program; the IF-DO-after-all-unconditional-invocations rule is not enforced across the caller/protocol boundary.

The tikhon binary on PATH is a site-packages install; lint/seal were run through it (digest matches the repo-source computation) and all runtime smoke checks ran against repo sources via PYTHONPATH=src.
